record.original_question: Determine the sharp regularity of generalized minimal flows within anisotropic function spaces tailored to flow-line geometry.

evidence.quote: Problem 17. Determine the true regularity of GM-flows in the framework of anisotropic function spaces.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $M$ be a compact Riemannian manifold (for concreteness, take $M = [0,1]^n$ with $n \ge 2$, or the flat torus $\mathbb{T}^n$). Denote by $\mathrm{SDiff}(M)$ the group of volume-preserving diffeomorphisms of $M$. Given two volume-preserving maps $\eta_0, \eta_1 \in \mathrm{SDiff}(M)$, consider the variational problem of minimizing the kinetic action
$$\mathcal{A}(\eta) \;=\; \tfrac{1}{2}\int_0^1\!\!\int_M |\partial_t \eta(t,x)|^2 \, dx\, dt$$
over paths $t \mapsto \eta(t,\cdot)$ joining $\eta_0$ to $\eta_1$. In general no classical minimizer exists, and one is led to Brenier's relaxation: a generalized minimal flow (GM-flow) is a probability measure $\mu$ on the space of continuous paths $\Omega = C([0,1], M)$ that is incompressible (the time-$t$ marginal of $\mu$ equals normalized volume for every $t \in [0,1]$), that satisfies the prescribed endpoint coupling $(e_0, e_1)_\# \mu = (\mathrm{id} \times \eta_1)_\# \mathrm{vol}$, and that minimizes the action
$$\mathcal{A}(\mu) \;=\; \int_\Omega\!\!\int_0^1 \tfrac{1}{2}|\dot\gamma(t)|^2\,dt\, d\mu(\gamma)$$
among all such measures. The associated pressure field $p$ is the Lagrange multiplier in the dual problem, and is known to be a distribution on $(0,1)\times M$ with limited Sobolev/BV regularity in space–time.

Problem. Introduce anisotropic function spaces $X^{s,s'}$ on $(0,1)\times M$ adapted to the geometry of flow lines — that is, spaces in which regularity is measured separately in directions tangent to the typical Lagrangian trajectories of the GM-flow and in directions transverse to them — and determine the sharp regularity, expressed by sharp exponents $(s, s')$, of:

(i) the pressure field $p$ associated to a GM-flow, and
(ii) the conditional law of trajectories $\gamma \mapsto \gamma(t)$ of $\mu$ along flow lines,

within these anisotropic spaces. The goal is to identify the optimal anisotropic Hölder/Sobolev/Besov scale on which GM-flows possess regularity strictly better than the known isotropic bounds.
artifact.status_search_result: No publication establishing sharp anisotropic regularity for generalized minimal (Brenier) flows was located. The known regularity results (e.g. Brenier's BV/Sobolev bounds on the pressure, and Ambrosio–Figalli-type refinements) are stated in isotropic spaces, and recent literature on anisotropic Lagrangian regularity addresses different vector-field problems. The problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Generalized fluid flows, their approximation and applications
status_evidence.snippet: Shnirelman's foundational work on generalized (relaxed) minimizing flows and their approximation.
status_evidence.claim: Defines the relaxed variational framework underlying GM-flows; does not give sharp anisotropic regularity.

status_evidence.title: Lagrangian flows for vector fields with anisotropic regularity
status_evidence.snippet: Develops theory of Lagrangian flows when some derivatives of some components are measures while others are integrable.
status_evidence.claim: Anisotropic regularity tools exist in related settings, but are not applied to determine sharp regularity of GM-flows.

status_evidence.title: Lecture notes on variational models for incompressible Euler equations
status_evidence.snippet: Surveys Brenier's relaxation and known regularity of the pressure field for generalized incompressible flows.
status_evidence.claim: Best-known regularity of GM-flow pressure is stated in isotropic spaces; sharp anisotropic regularity is not established.
